PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Meta.ConfigNote: Where the library is, how a plop is made, the generators that build an asset into a scene package (each with its defaults, from the cottage garden's own code), and the catalogue environment the factory draws every asset in.
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Meta.Source: Written 30-Oct-2026, v0.6.0 (the generators ported from 10__Import__ScenePackage's tree, plant, mound, spire and hedge)

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Libr.Note: The app reads the library through the local server when it is there (always current), and the index file beside the library when it is not (an installed app, offline, or a plain static server).
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Libr.RootNote: From the engine's root (the folder holding 02__Src__AppModules), resolved from the engine's own files rather than the page (v0.8.2): a wrapper that pins the engine pins the library beside it in the same layout, and reads it with no change here
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Libr.MaxPlacedNote: Placed assets a drawing holds: each is rebuilt into the scene on every change

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Plac.Note: A plop: where it lands, which way it faces and how much it varies. The asset's own Placement section decides Facing, ScaleJitter and NewShapeEachPlop; these are the engine's limits round them.
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Plac.ScaleClampNote: However a plop is scaled, it stays this side of half and twice its size
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Plac.GroundYNote: Assets stand on the ground plane: the lawn is y = 0 everywhere the garden is

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Stag.Note: The catalogue environment the factory renders each asset in: the asset alone at the origin, as authored (its stage seed, no rotation, scale 1), on a disc of lawn, in a fixed light, so every thumbnail is drawn the same way.
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Stag.StageVersionNote: Bump when the stage changes: a thumbnail records the stage it was drawn on
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Stag.GroundRadiusFactorNote: The disc reaches this many times the asset's own half-spread: a patch of ground under it, paper all round
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Stag.FootprintNote: No building stands on the stage: the wash's darkening round a footprint is measured from a box nothing is near

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Config__Gene.Note: Each generator builds one kind of asset from its parameters (metres) and its own seed, exactly as the cottage garden builds its trees, borders and furniture. An asset's DAT names its generator and overrides any of these defaults.

Tree.Note: A broadleaf tree: a leaning trunk, a crown of lumpy masses (or a dome, wider than tall, as the apple), and branches drawn partly through the canopy

Conifer.Note: A yew-like conifer: a short trunk and a stack of masses narrowing to the top

Mound.Note: A shrub or a border plant: one crowning mass and a ring of others, domed (the cottage's mound)

Spire.Note: A hollyhock or a foxglove: a leaning stack of small masses, its stem drawn up through them

Hedge.Note: A clipped hedge: masses in a run along its length (x), its face to the front (+z)

Topiary.Note: A clipped cone: masses stacked from a broad base to a point

Grass.Note: An ornamental grass: a low crown and tapering blades leaning with the wind

Reeds.Note: Reeds at a margin: a narrow crown and upright blades, drawn as grass is

Planter.Note: A terracotta planter of ornamental grass: a flared pot with a band below its rim, the grass on top

PottedStandard.Note: A ball standard in a square lead planter (v0.8.12): a Versailles box with a plinth, a lip and a raised panel on each face (a bead inside its edge, a rosette at its middle), a clear stem, a clipped ball of tight masses drawn in the Topiary hand, and a tuft of strap leaves at the stem's foot drawn as pen strokes, those past the lip hanging over it (UnderplantLeaves 0: bare soil). StemM is the clear stem from the rim to the foot of the head. Overdraw and Wobble are the asset's own hand: how its pen sketches over its planting, multiplying the field's

Bench.Note: A timber garden bench: seat, back and four legs, its front to +z

PicketFence.Note: A panel of white picket fence: two posts with caps, two rails, pointed pickets at the front
